steps.say: Groin hernias are described in two languages that decide the operation. Nyhus grades one to four by the wall defect, while the European system maps lateral, medial and femoral zones with a three centimetre size cutoff. Big defects need wider mesh overlap. Speaking one of these languages keeps the notes and the plan consistent.
steps.tx: **Nyhus** types **I to IV** (posterior-wall defect grades) plus **EHS classification** (lateral-medial-femoral zones) with a **3** cm size split standardise how groin hernias are described and which mesh is chosen. Large defects need wider overlap, and femoral zone defects change the approach.

vis.caption: Examination maps landmarks and types before Nyhus grading. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The open mesh repair named after Lichtenstein remains the world standard. A six by eleven centimetre polypropylene sheet reinforces the whole floor without stitching tissues under tension. Keyhole alternatives go behind the wall, with one staying out of the belly cavity and the other suiting both sided or recurrent hernias.
steps.tx: Open **Lichtenstein** repair lays a **6 by 11** cm polypropylene sheet tension-free as the enduring standard, while **TEP** (totally extraperitoneal, avoiding peritoneal breach) and **TAPP** (transabdominal preperitoneal, aiding bilateral and recurrent cases) place mesh behind the wall. Keyhole repairs trade scars for posterior mesh.

vis.alt: Operative drawing of Lichtenstein hernioplasty with mesh in the inguinal canal.
vis.caption: Lichtenstein lays mesh over the whole floor without tension. Credit: Doctoroftcm.

steps.say: The small lump below the groin crease in an older woman deserves special fear, because the femoral ring is narrow and rigid. Four in ten are already strangulated when first seen. Plugs are forbidden here since they wander into vessels, so the ring is closed to the Cooper ligament or covered from behind with flat mesh.
steps.tx: **Femoral hernia** (bulge below the crease through a tight opening) with its rigid ring obstructs blood supply in **40** percent by first presentation, needing **McVay** repair to Cooper ligament (stitching to the pectineal band) or preperitoneal mesh rather than inguinal plug. Plugs migrate into femoral vessels.

steps.say: The athlete with groin pain on twisting and kicking may have torn the tendon above the pubic bone rather than a true hernia. Six weeks of physio with a pubic injection comes first, with scans confirming the tear. Only failures go to theatre, where mesh backs up the weakened wall and the adductor is released if tight.
steps.tx: **Sports hernia** (athletic pubalgia with groin pain) with a torn **conjoint tendon** (fused internal oblique and transversus insertion) plus sore adductors in athletes earns mesh reinforcement following **6** weeks of failed physiotherapy with symphyseal injection. Tears are confirmed on MRI before surgery.

steps.say: Pain that outlives the operation by months usually means a trapped nerve, not a failed repair. The ilioinguinal nerve is the usual victim, caught in stitches or mesh. A numbing injection at the trigger point both proves and often cures it. Stubborn cases need all three groin nerves divided through the keyhole.
steps.tx: Chronic post-herniorrhaphy pain past **3** months from **ilioinguinal** (groin skin nerve) entrapment starts with trigger-point injection, then laparoscopic **triple neurectomy** (dividing ilioinguinal, iliohypogastric and genitofemoral nerves) for failures unmoved by blocks after two failed blocks. Mesh explantation stays rare and absolutely last.

steps.say: Dead bowel in a groin hernia is the exception to every rule. Contaminated fields forbid plastic mesh, so the dead gut comes out and the hole is stitched with the patient's own tissue. The definitive mesh waits for a clean second sitting months later. Biological meshes are kept for narrow exceptions only.
steps.tx: **Strangulated hernia** (ischaemic bowel trapped in the sac) with bowel compromise gets resection with **suture repair** (native tissue stitching) in a dirty field, shunning plastic mesh, with mesh deferred to a clean second sitting. Biologic mesh is reserved for select contaminated cases with no alternative.

steps.say: Keyhole surgery sometimes finds a second hernia hiding on the quiet side, in one patient out of ten. Finding it is fixing it, since the camera is already there. At the other extreme, the fit elderly patient with a barely noticeable bulge can simply be watched, accepting a one percent yearly strangulation risk that rarely materialises.
steps.tx: **Occult contralateral hernia** (hidden second-side bulge) found in **10** percent gets fixed during the same TAPP, while **watchful waiting** (planned observation) fits minimally symptomatic groin hernias in the fit elderly carrying **1** percent yearly strangulation. Crossover stays low with counselling and yearly review.

steps.say: Every mesh consent is covering two injuries patients fear most. The testicular blood supply runs through the operating field and can clot, and the ejaculation nerves pass nearby. Modern lightweight wide pore meshes cut chronic pain against old heavyweight sheets. Gentle cord handling prevents both complications.
steps.tx: Testicular ischaemia and **dysejaculation** (painful or dry ejaculation from nerve injury) are consented mesh risks discussed before every repair, and **lightweight mesh** (large-pore light polypropylene) reduces chronic pain against heavyweight mesh. Cord structures are always spared during careful dissection in theatre.
